sources.limits: Generalized educational political map, not a surveyed hydronym-boundary product. Dense lower-river place labels obscure some fine network detail. Exact source, junction, floodplain-channel and tidal boundaries are not resolved. No publication year is asserted from file metadata. Original map and derivatives remain private.

sources.title: Geological map of Greenland 1:2 500 000
sources.authors: Jan C. Escher and T. Christopher R. Pulvertaft
sources.publisher: Geological Survey of Greenland (GGU); official digital copy hosted by GEUS
sources.page: Single map sheet, PDF page 1; northern Inland Ice, graticule, Victoria Fjord regional setting and Inland Ice legend

sources.limits: Regional geological mapping, not a river gazetteer or hydrological survey. It supports the feature-class scope conclusion, not proof of natural flow, connectivity or formal river identity. The historical ice margin is not asserted to be its current position.
sources.reuse_limit: GEUS custom terms allow internal research but restrict redistribution and new maps based on the data. The original map and local crops remain private; only own factual notes and public bibliography are intended for publication.

sources.title: Greenland from Archaean to Quaternary: Descriptive text to the 1995 Geological map of Greenland, 1:2 500 000, 2nd edition

sources.supports: Explains ice-contour classes and locates the mapped Victoria Fjord label, without establishing a natural river identity for the modeled path.
sources.limits: General glaciology and a map-label register cannot establish a name for the complete modeled river group. No present-day ice dimensions, margin position or melt-rate estimate is inferred from this historical report.

correspondence.finding: The southern modeled start lies west of Amarante do Maranhão and follows the long north-running corridor directly labeled Rio Pindaré on IBGE's map. Its slight westward bow and subsequent northeast turn agree with the mapped upper river. The Tocantins to the west, Açailândia tributary farther northwest and Grajaú drainage to the east remain distinct. The map does not establish the exact natural spring or initial named vertex.

The route turns northeast past the Buriticupu setting and continues toward Alto Alegre do Pindaré, following the same distinctive course and sequence of surrounding towns shown by IBGE. This route differs from the separate northward Zutiua corridor farther east. Fragment boundaries do not establish natural hydronym transitions.

The lower mainstem first runs generally east from Alto Alegre do Pindaré, then turns northeast through the Pindaré-Mirim/Santa Inês setting and continues by Monção. IBGE depicts this connected sequence. SEMA's station inventory independently places Alto Alegre do Pindaré, Tufilândia, Pindaré-Mirim, Monção and Cajari stations along the corresponding lower regional corridor. These are station-location corroboration, not a river-name field assigning every station or intervening line to Pindaré.

The long eastern contribution begins east of the upper Pindaré, trends northeast past the western side of the Arame setting and then north past Santa Luzia before meeting the mainstem near Pindaré-Mirim. This matches IBGE's separately labeled Rio Zutiua corridor. It is contributing-river context and is not renamed Pindaré or confused with the farther-east Grajaú; the exact beginning of its hydronym is unassigned.

The final northeast continuation reaches the inland lower Pindaré–Mearim junction setting north of the Vitória do Mearim/Arari corridor, rather than extending to the Atlantic coast. IBGE shows the lower network in this setting. The federal waterway account identifies Pindaré as a Mearim tributary and defines its lower section from Pindaré-Mirim to the Mearim. Generalized mapping and overlapping place labels do not fix the exact terminal confluence vertex, tidal boundary or individual floodplain channels.

The eastern endpoint and its long southwest approach occupy the eastern Assinica secondary-drainage setting on the provincial hydrography map. The selected route proceeds toward the Opataca lake corridor instead of following the upper Broadback branch by Frotet and Labeau. The small initial feeder is not named by this review.

The modeled upper route matches the Opataca–Cachisca–Comencho–Assinica lake-chain setting. The original map distinguishes each lake, and the report describes Opataca draining to Cachisca, Cachisca to Comencho, and Comencho north into Assinica. These are separate lake names within the modeled route, not aliases of Rivière Broadback.

From Lac Assinica, the path makes the westward and then northward approach of Rivière Assinica to its junction with Broadback. The original map and hydrographic account distinguish the Assinica tributary from the west-trending Broadback trunk. The modeled mainstem label does not erase this name transition.

After the Assinica junction, the selected route runs west along Broadback, enters the Evans lake setting, turns north and northeast through the Giffard passage, and then bends west again. The hydrography map depicts this distinctive sequence separately from the Théodat and Coigne contributing basins and from Nemiscau in the Rupert drainage. Evans and Giffard retain their separate waterbody scope.

The lower selected piece corresponds to the sinuous westward Rivière Broadback shown on the 2021 reserve map between the separately labeled Rupert river to the north and Nottaway to the south. Its terminal approach is in the Rupert Bay coastal setting identified by the official reserve page. No exact surveyed river-mouth vertex, tidal channel or estuary boundary is assigned.

The northern western approach follows the eastward Awuna corridor north of Lookout Ridge, then passes the Lookout River junction before meeting Colville. Both maps distinguish Awuna from the southern Colville approach. The report independently identifies separate Awuna sites above Lookout and near its mouth. The model's mainstem role does not make Awuna a Colville synonym.

The long western non-mainstem corridor begins in the Thunder Creek approach, turns north and then east onto upper Colville, and continues past the Nuka, Kiligwa, Kuna and Ipnavik tributary settings toward the Awuna junction. The short adjoining fragment continues the same Colville corridor; it is not a separately named tributary merely because of its modeled role.

After the Awuna junction, the eastward trunk follows labeled Colville along the reserve's southern margin, bends southeast near the Killik approach, then turns northeast toward Umiat. These successive turns match the actual modeled path. Separate tributary labels on the maps are not extended over the trunk.

The Umiat reach continues northeast and then predominantly north across the coastal plain, beside the mapped Kogosukruk and Kikiakrorak contributing corridors. It remains west of the separate Itkillik River until their lower-river setting. The observed bend sequence, rather than the bounding box alone, supports Colville correspondence.

The final northward continuation reaches the western Colville delta setting by Nuiqsut and Harrison Bay. The detailed map shows multiple named channels there, so the group candidate does not assign every delta channel or a precise contemporary mouth. The report explicitly distinguishes the delta from its more restricted Special Area study corridor.

correspondence: The complete single selected fragment was inspected: a long nearly northward interior leg, a short north-northeast section, an eastward bend with a southward dip, then a final northern extension. No additional tributary fragment is present.

The long southern and middle route crosses mapped Inland Ice. The northern bends approach the ice-margin and inner Victoria Fjord regional setting, identified from the original graticule and surrounding ice, land and fjord configuration; the exact terminal natural-feature boundary is not assigned.

The readable original does not establish a natural river name for the full modeled route. Nearby fjord or glacier labels cannot supply a uniform river identity, nor does this scope hold mean every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.

The ice-surface contours, ice-thickness isopachs and sub-ice bedrock contours are terrain information rather than named river channels. Historical mapping does not establish present-day ice margins, subglacial connectivity or flow along the modeled line.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
